figures.finding: The minimum age of employment is eighteen; a child of thirteen to seventeen may be employed only in the categories of work and workplaces the rules and regulations under the Act list, and breaking either rule is a felony of the third degree. Under thirteen no employment is allowed.

value.from13: only in categories and workplaces listed in the rules

figures.applies: Nationwide; the rules listing the categories weren't reached (see blockers).

sources.said: 170. Minimum age of employment shall be 18 years. … 171. The employment of a child between 13 to 17 years of age shall be limited only to the categories of work and in workplaces as specified in the rules and regulation to this Act subject however, to the conditions laid down under section 9 172. A person who contravenes section 170 and 171 shall be guilty of an offence which shall be a felony of the third degree.

figures.finding: The Act has no performer's rule: a child under thirteen may not be employed in any work, performing included, and one of thirteen to seventeen only in the categories the rules list; whether acting is among them wasn't found. The same holds for a young writer or director employed.

value.13-17: only categories listed in the rules (not read)

figures.finding: A person is competent to contract only at the age of majority 'according to the law applicable to him or her', of sound mind and not disqualified by law; the Act doesn't itself fix that age, and no court-approval route for a minor's creative contract or any set-aside of earnings was found.

value.competence: age of majority under the applicable law (Contract Act s. 20)

sources.said: 20. A person shall be competent to enter into a contract if : (4) He or she is of the age of majority according to the law applicable to him or her; (5) He or she is of sound mind; and (6) He or she is not disqualified from contracting by any law in force in the Kingdom of Bhutan.

figures.finding: Bhutanese law treats every person under eighteen as a child (Child Care and Protection Act 2011, s. 16), and the Contract Act 2013 makes the capacity to contract turn on the age of majority by the law applicable to the person; no separate majority statute was found, so majority is read as eighteen.

value.law: Child Care and Protection Act of Bhutan 2011, s. 16; Contract Act of Bhutan 2013 (capacity: age of majority by the applicable law)

figures.applies: Everyone. The Companies Act 2016 (s. 51) also bars registering a share in the name of a person under eighteen. Bhutan has no general majority act; the age is read from the child-protection law's definition.

figures.finding: A person under eighteen cannot hold shares in their own name in a Bhutanese company (the share is registered to a guardian or trustee), and the Companies Act's list of persons who may not be directors names insolvents, convicts, persons of unsound mind, unpaid calls and more than three public boards, but no age.

value.directorNote: s. 141 sets no age; capacity otherwise by the Contract Act (age of majority)
value.law: Companies Act of Bhutan 2016, ss. 51 and 141

figures.applies: Every company under the Companies Act of Bhutan 2016. A minor's shares sit with the guardian or trustee until majority (s. 56 for nominees).
